prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: overpaying the mortgage. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member says they overpay “most months”, I should still ask for the exact amount and frequency, because regular standing overpayments are treated differently from ad hoc extra payments and can affect affordability and ERC checks."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a mortgage offers an overpayment allowance, I should verify whether the allowance is a percentage of the outstanding balance or an annual cash cap, because exceeding it can trigger early repayment charges or require a formal product review."},{"type":"observation","content":"When overpayments are funded from variable income such as bonuses, commission or overtime, I should treat them as optional rather than committed expenditure unless the member can show they are consistent and sustainable."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a remortgage is being arranged and the member wants to keep making overpayments, I should confirm that the new lender’s terms, payment method and cut-off dates will still allow the same pattern without penalties."},{"type":"fact","content":"When assessing affordability, I should not rely on projected overpayments to make the case fit, because the case must stand on the contractual payment and verified income before any extra repayments are considered."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member has been overpaying for a long time, I should check whether they want to reduce the term, reduce the monthly payment, or keep the term unchanged, because the intended outcome matters for the recommendation."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member’s savings buffer is thin, I should be cautious about recommending large overpayments, because keeping some cash back for emergencies is usually safer than accelerating the loan at the expense of resilience."},{"type":"observation","content":"When overpayments are made shortly before a remortgage, I should confirm whether they have already been reflected in the latest balance, because a stale statement can make the redemption figure and loan-to-value look wrong."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a fixed-rate product has a monthly overpayment limit, I should count all extra payments together, including payment rounding, one-off bank transfers and any extra direct debit amounts, because they all form part of the same overpayment total."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member’s aim is to pay the mortgage off sooner, I should explain that overpaying now can shorten the term significantly, but only if the extra payments are maintained and the product terms do not change."}]}
